anomalies.observed: All four bus-pin select jumpers (R22, R24, R19, R4) are 0 Ω and all are populated in the netlist. R22 and R24 both join the ch.1 PWM net /NET0030 to bus pins /NET0015 (pin 21) and /NET0027 (pin 19), so bus pins 19 and 21 are bridged together. R19 and R4 do the same for bus pins 20 and 22 on /NET0017.
anomalies.expected: The spec says exactly one pair is shorted per core variant ('Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others'). Each channel should connect to only one of its two candidate bus pins, so the two M5Stack GPIOs are not shorted together.

evidence.quote: R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2 — schematic note: "Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others"

anomalies.impact: If the jumpers are populated as the netlist shows, two different M5Stack bus GPIOs drive the same servo line. On the wrong core variant the GPIO outputs contend, which can damage the core IO or the servo signal, and the wrong pin is driven.

anomalies.observed: R1 is 2.2k. It sits in the B-line bias divider with R10 (2.2k from +3V3), so B is held near mid-rail.
anomalies.expected: The spec gives R1 as 10k, the bias/divider from /TXD2 into Q2's base, and R8 as 2.2k. The netlist instead has R8 at 10k and R1 at 2.2k.

evidence.quote: | R1, R2 | 10k, 5.1k | Bias/divider from `/TXD2` into Q2's base. |

anomalies.impact: The bias network on the transceiver lines differs from the intended design. It changes the idle state of the B line and the drive into the direction-control transistor, so bus idle and fail-safe behaviour may not match what was intended.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows all four 0 Ω bus-select jumpers populated, which bridges bus pins 19/21 and 20/22 together, contrary to the spec's one-pair-per-variant rule. Several resistor values also disagree with the spec, though the spec's reference naming is inconsistent enough that those are only weakly supported.
